name: Anthropic Claude Opus 5 — 1M Context, $5/$25, 96% SWE-bench Verified; Now Default Opus in Claude Code
hook: Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5 on July 24, 2026, and it became the default Opus model in Claude Code that same day via v2.1.219. It scores 96.0% on SWE-bench Verified and 79.2% on SWE-bench Pro — more than doubling Opus 4.8's per-task performance — and hits 3× the next-best model on ARC-AGI 3 at unchanged pricing ($5 input / $25 output per MTok). A flat 1M-token context window with thinking on by default; fast mode runs at $10/$50 at 2.5× speed. Also hits SOTA on OSWorld 2.0 GUI interaction and 1.5× Opus 4.8's pass rate on Zapier AutomationBench.

name: anthropics/ralph-wiggum — Official Anthropic Loop Plugin; 139K Stars; Stop Hook Keeps Claude Working Until Done
hook: Ralph Wiggum is the official Anthropic autonomous-loop plugin inside the claude-code repo: a Stop hook blocks Claude's exit, re-injects the original prompt, and loops until Claude outputs a configurable completion phrase (e.g., `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>`) or hits `--max-iterations`. Concrete benefit: you can hand it a greenfield REST API spec and walk away — Claude reads its own git history and file output each iteration to improve, catches its own test failures, and only stops when done. 139K stars, 22.3K forks. r/ClaudeAI flagged it as viral this week.

name: ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp — Official Chrome Team MCP; 47.6K Stars; 29 Tools for Browser Debugging in Claude Code
hook: The Chrome DevTools team's official MCP server gives Claude Code (and any MCP client) direct access to a live Chrome browser through 29 tools: browser automation with clicks, form fills, navigation, and dialogs; Lighthouse audits; performance traces; memory snapshots; network request inspection; and console-message analysis. 47.6K stars as of July 24. WhiteBoard Coder ran a hands-on test with Claude and chrome-devtools-mcp in July 2026, noting that Claude can open URLs, click through UI, and pull performance metrics without a separate testing framework.

name: Claude Code v2.1.219 (July 24) — DirectoryAdded Hook; sandbox.network.strictAllowlist; Depth-3 Subagents
hook: Beyond landing Claude Opus 5 as the default, v2.1.219 ships three notable engineering additions. `DirectoryAdded` hook fires whenever `/add-dir` or the SDK `register_repo_root` registers a new working directory mid-session — lets hooks react to scope changes in large monorepo workflows. `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` denies all non-allowlisted hosts for sandboxed commands without prompting, giving teams a hard network-egress control. And nested subagents can now spawn their own subagents up to depth 3 (was 1), enabling three-tier orchestration trees without manual forwarding. Also adds `workflowSizeGuideline` as a settable key.

name: alirezarezvani/claude-skills — 345 Skills; 30+ Agents; 70+ Commands; Works Across 13 Coding Agents
hook: A single install drops 345 production-ready agent skills, 30+ specialist agents, and 70+ custom commands into your ~/.claude directory — covering engineering, marketing, product, compliance, C-level advisory, finance, DevOps, and personal productivity. Hit #1 GitHub Trending on July 5, 2026; 15.3K stars as of July 14. Uniquely cross-platform: the same SKILL.md files work across Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, Kilo Code, OpenCode, Augment Code, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Mistral Vibe, and Antigravity with zero conversion.

name: SawyerHood/dev-browser — Browser Automation Skill; QuickJS WASM Sandbox; Persistent Page State; 6.5K Stars
hook: Gives Claude Code a real browser without the security concerns: scripts execute inside a QuickJS WASM sandbox with no access to the host filesystem or network, while the browser itself connects to a running Chrome or fresh Chromium. Features persistent page state across steps (so Claude can log in once and reuse the session), step-by-step debug mode, smart DOM analysis, and Chrome extension support. 6.5K stars; recently featured in the hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code curated list. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and any agent that reads skill files.

name: Graphify-Labs/graphify — ~95K Stars; Day 3; Knowledge Graph for Any Codebase; 70x Cost Cut
hook: Turns any codebase — plus docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs — into a queryable knowledge graph using local deterministic AST parsing (tree-sitter, 158 languages). A PreToolUse hook routes every file-search through the graph; 15 MCP tools add path tracing, dead-code detection, and architecture analysis. MindStudio benchmarks show up to 70x cost reduction on 500+ file projects. v0.9.25 added automatic diff-impact analysis and Figma-node support. Continues to hold position as the leading codebase-graph tool in the Claude Code ecosystem.
install: uv tool install graphifyy && graphify install
recurring_note: ↑ Day 3 — ~95K stars; codebase-graph category still accelerating

name: multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills — 194K+ Stars; Day 8; 4 Rules That Stop Claude Breaking Code
hook: A CLAUDE.md encoding Andrej Karpathy's four rules for LLM coding: Think Before Coding, Simplicity First, Surgical Changes, Goal-Driven Execution. Each rule blocks a specific failure mode Karpathy documented — unfounded assumptions, unnecessary abstraction, unintended side-effects, vague success criteria. 194K+ stars; the most-cited CLAUDE.md framework in the ecosystem this week. Works as a drop-in CLAUDE.md or installable plugin across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and 60+ other agents. With Opus 5's sharper reasoning, many users are pairing this with the new model today.
recurring_note: ↑ Day 8 — 194K+ stars; still the dominant CLAUDE.md framework

name: JuliusBrussee/caveman — 92.3K Stars; Day 2; 65% Fewer Output Tokens; Caveman-Speak, Full Accuracy
hook: Compresses agent responses into terse caveman-speak without losing any technical accuracy — code, commands, and error messages remain byte-for-byte exact, only the prose is stripped. Benchmarked at 65% average output token reduction (range 22–87% across 1,200 test scenarios). Output tokens are typically 1–2% of a Claude Code bill, so the gains are largest for output-heavy automation. 92.3K stars, 5.2K forks. Pairs naturally with Claude Opus 5 today: faster output + longer context means caveman's compression keeps costs predictable on big-context runs.
recurring_note: ↑ 92.3K stars; pairing with Opus 5 for output-cost control

name: farion1231/cc-switch — 120K Stars; Day 2; Desktop GUI Switches Between 6 Coding Agents; 50+ Provider Presets
hook: Cross-platform desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux) that eliminates hand-editing JSON and environment files when switching between Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent. One click swaps between 50+ API provider presets; a unified sidebar manages MCP servers and Skills across all tools simultaneously; cloud sync keeps configs consistent across machines. v3.18.0 released July 21. With Claude Opus 5 now the default Opus, cc-switch users can hot-swap the model per-agent from one panel. 120K stars, 8.1K forks.
recurring_note: ↑ 120K stars; Opus 5 default makes model-switching more relevant

name: thedotmack/claude-mem — 88.3K Stars; Day 2; Persistent Memory Across Sessions; 5 Hooks + SQLite + Chroma
hook: Solves session amnesia with five lifecycle hooks (SessionStart, PostToolUse, Stop, UserPromptSubmit, SessionEnd) that capture every tool use, file read, and edit; a local Bun worker compresses observations via Claude Agent SDK and stores them in SQLite with full-text search and Chroma for hybrid semantic/keyword retrieval. Future sessions surface relevant memories with visible token costs via the mem-search skill's 'progressive disclosure' system. v13.12.2 shipped July 23; 88.3K stars. With Opus 5's 1M context window, claude-mem's memory injection becomes less of a context-pressure problem.
recurring_note: ↑ 88.3K stars; 1M Opus 5 context changes how mem-injection feels
